question: Why does it lose, and what would make it profitable?
dataset: NFO/BFO futures, continuous daily 2018-2026, 362 symbols, real exchange lot sizes

position_sizing_correction.finding: An earlier run used qty=1, which is not a tradable size — the minimum is one LOT (20..71,475 here, median 600). Brokerage plus GST is ~Rs 47 per round trip and does NOT scale with size, so qty=1 charged a whole fee against one unit of notional.
position_sizing_correction.effect: Correcting it does NOT rescue the strategy. Lot sizing is close to equal-NOTIONAL weighting; unit sizing over-weights expensive names. On the correct basis the best long cell goes from gross +13,006 (qty=1) to gross -2,386,766 (lots).

exit_mode_sweep.finding: Looser exits are consistently BETTER than the shipped one_red, and holding longer is worse. Best long: three_red with exit_aligned_trail OFF (gross -2.39M vs one_red -7.36M). exit_aligned_trail ON holds ~36 bars and gives the edge back (-7.29M). three_red and three_red_signal are identical because the trail fires first.
exit_mode_sweep.short_side: Catastrophic in every cell: -9.98M to -39.01M gross. Not a tuning problem.

entry_forward_return.method: Open-to-open forward return after a fresh alignment, vs the base rate of all bars.
entry_forward_return.finding: The entry has NEGATIVE alpha. A long signal underperforms a random bar by 26 bps; price RISES 366 bps after a bear signal, so the short side is strongly anti-predictive. Three-line agreement on Heikin-Ashi is a late confirmation: by the time all three agree, the move is over. No exit tuning fixes negative entry alpha — that is arithmetic.

inverted_hypothesis.rule: Buy the BEAR alignment. Fixed 20-bar hold, next-open in and out, lot-sized, futures costs at 0.0002 slippage.
inverted_hypothesis.note: The engine's own exits cannot express this: they are defined against the alignment that opened the trade, so an entry taken against alignment closes on the next bar (gross exactly 0). It needs a different exit, so it is a different strategy.
honest_reading: About half the return is market DRIFT: random entries in the same symbols and window returned 6.73M. The signal's own contribution is ~7.06M at z=+3.01.
The hypothesis was generated FROM this data — the forward-return table spanned 2018-2026 including the 2025+ holdout. This is in-sample, not out-of-sample.
Roughly 30 configurations have now been tested. Nominal two-sided p from z=3.01 is 0.0026; a Bonferroni-style correction over that search puts it near 0.08. Not significant at 5%.
The control randomises entry TIMING but not the fact that bear alignments cluster in drawdowns. Buying dips in a bull market is a known beta-timing effect.
Verdict: SUGGESTIVE, NOT ESTABLISHED. It is a lead to test on data this hypothesis has never seen, not a strategy to fund.

recommendation: Do not trade the current logic in any configuration. Entry alpha is negative on both sides.
Delete the short side outright: -191 bps of alpha per signal, worst cell in every sweep.
If the engine is kept, three_red with exit_aligned_trail OFF is strictly better than the shipped one_red — but better here means losing less, not making money.
The only positive lead is fading the signal rather than following it, with a fixed-horizon exit. That is a new strategy and needs its own forward-collected holdout before it means anything.
